title: Billing Optimistic Count
prompt: A React billing item applies an optimistic toggle before the server responds. Write a helper that flips selected and adjusts selectedCount up or down by 1.

explanation.beginner:
Example: billingOptimisticCount({"id":"1","selected":false,"selectedCount":4}) produces {"id":"1","selected":true,"selectedCount":5}. The result must follow this precise rule: A React billing item applies an optimistic toggle before the server responds. Write a helper that flips selected and adjusts selectedCount up or down by 1. Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Compare “decrements when unselecting”: input [{"id":"1","selected":true,"selectedCount":4}] produces {"id":"1","selected":false,"selectedCount":3}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.

Tempting mistake: Do not hard-code the first example: the decrements when unselecting case changes the input contract’s boundary or shape. Compare the actual outputs rather than only checking whether both are truthy.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “decrements when unselecting”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
